title: Implement minimal Block prototype
body:
## Goal

Design and implement the minimal interface required for a Mosaic Block in C++.

## Context

Project Mosaic is built around composable Blocks that can be connected into graphs and eventually compiled into an executable representation. We need to implement a small, working foundation to test the block creation standard.

## Tasks

- Identify the minimum information a Block needs (ID, type, ports).
- Define how inputs and outputs are represented.
- Create a small C++ prototype of the interface.
- Document the major design decisions (stateful vs stateless blocks).

## Expected result

A minimal C++ Block interface implementation with a small example block and test case.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome.

title: Implement minimal Graph data structure
body:
## Goal

Implement a minimal graph representation capable of storing Mosaic Blocks and their connections.

## Context

Mosaic uses graphs to represent relationships between composable Blocks. Before compilation or execution can happen, we need a reliable representation of this graph.

## Tasks

- Implement a minimal Graph class supporting adding/removing nodes (Blocks).
- Support connecting block outputs to inputs.
- Implement basic traversal methods.

## Expected result

A small, self-contained Graph implementation in C++ with unit tests.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. Consider how nodes are identified, how connections are represented, and whether the graph should own its Blocks.

title: Add graph validation
body:
## Goal

Create a validation system that can detect invalid Mosaic graphs before compilation/execution.

## Context

A graph should be validated before it reaches later stages of the pipeline. Validation should catch structural problems early, such as cycles, missing required ports, or type mismatches.

## Tasks

- Detect connections referencing nonexistent nodes/ports.
- Check for missing required inputs.
- Implement cycle detection in the graph.

## Expected result

A validation pass that inspects a graph and returns safety status.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. Consider whether cycles are always invalid and how multiple validation errors should be reported.

title: Prototype Graph → IR conversion
body:
## Goal

Create a small prototype that converts a validated Mosaic graph into an intermediate representation (IR).

## Context

One of Mosaic's central ideas is separating the user-facing graph from the representation used for compilation and execution. The IR should provide a cleaner representation for later optimization and scheduling.

## Tasks

- Define a minimal IR representation (e.g. instructions/linear ops).
- Map Blocks to IR instructions.
- Preserve dependencies during conversion.

## Expected result

A minimal working Graph → IR converter in C++ or Python with at least one demonstrated example.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. Consider whether the IR should be graph-based, instruction-based, or hybrid.

title: Prototype dependency scheduler
body:
## Goal

Create a prototype that determines a valid execution order for dependent Mosaic nodes.

## Context

A Mosaic graph describes relationships between operations, but the runtime eventually needs a scheduled execution order.

## Tasks

- Implement a basic topological scheduling algorithm.
- Detect cycles and report them gracefully.
- Produce a deterministic schedule.

## Expected result

A small scheduler prototype that accepts a dependency graph/IR and produces a valid execution plan.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. Consider whether independent nodes should be allowed to execute in parallel and whether scheduling should happen on the Graph or IR.

title: Create minimal 2D proof-of-concept
body:
## Goal

Create a tiny runnable example demonstrating how Mosaic's architecture can represent a simple 2D game/system.

## Context

Mosaic is ultimately intended to support game development, so we need small practical examples that test whether the architecture is actually useful and identify any architectural friction early.

## Tasks

- Define the Blocks required for the example (e.g. Input → Movement → Transform → Render).
- Construct and execute the corresponding graph.
- Document what the example demonstrates.

## Expected result

A small runnable C++ or Python example showing a simple 2D pipeline represented using Mosaic.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. The goal is NOT to create a complete game, but to expose useful architectural insights.

title: Design graph diagnostics/error reporting
body:
## Goal

Design a diagnostics system to report validation errors, structural issues, and type mismatches.

## Context

A validated graph needs useful, actionable diagnostics so developers know exactly which blocks and ports are causing validation failures. Naive return codes or generic exceptions are not sufficient for a modular engine.

## Tasks

- Define a diagnostic data structure (e.g. severity, error code, location, message).
- Define how location refers to blocks, connections, or specific ports.
- Implement a basic reporter that converts diagnostic objects into clean string messages.
- Provide an example of reporting multiple diagnostics at once.

## Expected result

A design and minimal prototype of a diagnostics utility that validates a graph and reports precise, human-readable error messages.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome.

title: Investigate parallel execution model
body:
## Goal

Research and design how independent blocks can run in parallel on multi-threaded CPUs or GPU pipelines.

## Context

Composable graphs expose natural concurrency since blocks with satisfied dependencies can be scheduled in parallel. We need to determine how the compiler and runtime should model task parallelism without introducing locks or execution overhead.

## Tasks

- Research task scheduling libraries (e.g., Intel TBB, Taskflow, custom thread pools).
- Draft a proposal for mapping independent IR nodes to thread pool tasks.
- Consider how data is passed between threads without race conditions.
- Document performance trade-offs of runtime scheduling vs static compilation scheduling.

## Expected result

A design document describing a potential parallel execution model for block scheduling.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome.

title: Investigate Vulkan/backend boundary
body:
## Goal

Investigate how a Vulkan backend can coexist with other execution backends without leaking graphics implementation details into the core API.

## Context

Mosaic is intended to support replaceable systems/backends. Vulkan is one potential graphics backend, but the engine architecture should avoid becoming tightly coupled to Vulkan-specific concepts.

## Tasks

- Research and document what the core graphics abstraction should expose.
- Define how resources, command submission, and synchronization should be represented.
- Propose a clean boundary separating core graph compilation from backend execution.

## Expected result

A short technical design/research document describing a possible Vulkan backend architecture.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. A conclusion that a particular approach is a bad idea is a valid result.

title: Create architecture test suite
body:
## Goal

Create a collection of small tests that verify Mosaic's core architectural assumptions.

## Context

Because Mosaic is experimental, tests are useful not only for preventing regressions but also for determining whether the architecture behaves as expected.

## Tasks

- Create unit tests for block creation and port definitions.
- Create integration tests verifying graph construction, validation, IR conversion, and scheduling.
- Ensure tests run automatically as part of the normal development workflow.

## Expected result

A small suite of tests that exercise the fundamental Mosaic pipeline.

## Notes

This is an architectural experiment. Alternative approaches are welcome. Tests should be small and easy to understand.
